 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. DALLAS - The Houston Rockets play their first NBA Cup game Friday night against the Dallas Mavericks at American Airlines Center.
 The Rockets are in Group A along with the Mavericks, Denver Nuggets, Phoenix Suns and Utah Jazz. Each team will play a game against the other teams in their group. The top team in each of the six groups and two wild cards (the best second-place team in each conference) will advance to the knockout rounds.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Coach Ime Udoka said the in-season tournament offers "added incentive," but more than anything, he wants his 5-0 team to continue playing good basketball. 
 "It adds some to it, and we know there's a goal at the end of the line on this, but we're playing good and we want to continue that regardless," he said.
 Houston has qualified for the knockout round once in Udoka's tenure. The Rockets made the semifinal in his second season before losing to the eventual champion Oklahoma City Thunder.
 The Rockets will have starting point guard Fred VanVleet against Dallas. The veteran, coming off a torn ACL, is only playing in one half of Houston's back-to-backs, meaning he will almost certainly miss the Rockets' Saturday night matchup with the Oklahoma City Thunder at Toyota Center.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Udoka said that if the Rockets were fully healthy, he'd likely look to stagger VanVleet and Steven Adams on either half of back-to-backs depending on matchups. However, Houston isn't healthy - Adams is out with a right calf strain, starting center Alperen Şengün and Reed Sheppard are out with lower back soreness.
 Marcus Smart, who was questionable with a left forearm strain, will play against Dallas. Udoka said the uncertainty of Smart's and Sheppard's availability was the primary reason he chose to play VanVleet against the Mavericks.
 Last year's NBA Cup champion, the New York Knicks, were initially not going to raise a banner for their victory but decided to do so after winning the NBA Finals. Udoka, asked his preference on raising a banner if Houston won the NBA Cup, kept it simple.
 "I don't care."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Rockets pick up Reed Sheppard's contract option
 The Rockets announced Friday that they picked up the fourth-year option for Sheppard, an expected move that keeps the No. 3 pick in the 2024 draft under contract through the 2027-28 season.
 Sheppard played all 82 games last season, starting 21 games and averaging 13.5 points, 3.4 assists and 1.5 steals per game. The guard becomes eligible for an extension this offseason.
